chunks: And if Allah, the Glorified, had wished for His prophets, at the time He sent them, to open for them treasures of gold, mines of precious stones, and plantations of gardens, and to gather around them the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth, He would have done so,
And if He had done so, then the trial would have fallen away, and the recompense would have been nullified, and the tidings (of the Hereafter) would have faded away,
and the recompense due to those who accepted (the message) after trial would not have become obligatory, and the believers would not have deserved the reward for the doers of good,
and the names would not have retained their meanings,

But Allah, the Glorified, made His messengers firm in their determination, and weak in what the eyes see of their states, along with contentment that fills the hearts and eyes with richness, and poverty that fills the sights and ears with affliction.
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah make the Prophets poor and weak if He could have given them wealth?
ai.summary: Shia scholars, such as Ibn Abi al-Hadid, interpret this passage as highlighting the 'test of poverty' (ibtila' al-faqar) as a deliberate divine strategy to preserve the authenticity of prophetic mission and the merit of human choice. By maintaining outward vulnerability, the Prophets ensured that their spiritual authority was not conflated with worldly power, thereby validating the rewards for those who endure hardship with patience. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the Imamate and Prophethood as roles defined by spiritual resilience rather than material accumulation.
